name: Cerrejonisuchus
sum: Small short-snouted dyrosaurid from the Paleocene of Colombia, with the shortest estimated body length of any known dyrosaur.
holotype: UF/IGM 29, a complete skull from the Cerrejón Formation, Colombia.
material: Other specimens are UF/IGM 30 (lower jaw), UF/IGM 31 (skull and partial postcranial skeleton) and UF/IGM 32 (snout).
biology: The rostrum is only 54–59% of skull length, the shortest of all dyrosaurids; well-developed osteoderms suggest the animals were mature.
author: Hastings et al. 2010

sources.text: Hastings, A. K 2010. A new small short-snouted dyrosaurid (Crocodylomorpha, Mesoeucrocodylia) from the Paleocene of northeastern Colombia. Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology 30(1): 139–162. doi:10.1080/02724630903409204
